A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RA-RAG research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. Appendix renumbering and relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and real-world source-reliability estimates in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical outcomes, including QA benchmark results, filtering analyses, computational measurements, and evaluations of political claims and social-media posts.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same iterative reliability estimation, AlignScore filtering, semantic clustering, weighted majority voting, and κ-RRSS procedure. No algorithmic component or model behavior is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same NQ, TriviaQA, and single-hop HotpotQA coverage, synthetic reliability scenarios, and real-world sources comprising Politician A, Politician B, and User A. The benchmark description moves from Appendix H to G without changing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Oracle WMV, MV, Vanilla RAG, Robust RAG, Self-RAG, and Vanilla LLM where originally evaluated. Self-RAG remains in the Llama2-7B experiments, and the runtime and κ-RSS comparisons retain their original comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported settings remain identical, including the 200/1,400 estimation/test split, the separate 800/800 filtering experiment, model configurations, reliability priors, retrieval depths, κ = 4, and evaluation metrics. Real-world sampling and top-20 retrieval settings also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The κ sensitivity, relevance-selection, κ-RRSS removal, filtering, threshold-sensitivity, and qualitative case analyses are retained with the same evidence. Appendix renumbering does not add or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over 10 random trials in Section 5.1 and retain the same PCC/SRCC significance reporting in Figures 5 and A9. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted results, and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table A4 retains NQ RA-RAG accuracy of 0.558 with seven adversaries, and Table 3 retains source-level accuracies of 0.949, 0.932, and 0.795.

T1.justification: The source-partition, aggregation, filtering, clustering, and reliability-estimation definitions and Equations (1)–(6) are unchanged. Neither version adds or removes a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same substantive contribution and performance claims. Section 2 adds an explicit, qualified claim that this is the first work to embed reliability estimation for robust information in RAG, modestly strengthening the novelty claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reliability weighting, filtering, scalability, and real-world accuracy remain unchanged. Both versions retain limitations concerning specialized topics, insufficient corroborating sources, offline reliability updates, and sudden source compromise, together with the same proposed extensions.

D1.justification: Both PDFs disclose the same generation prompts, corpus-construction procedures, filtering threshold, retriever and clustering models, RTX 6000 Ada hardware, runtime information, and code/data access link. Relocation and appendix renumbering introduce no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a brief discussion connecting RA-RAG to learning from noisy sources, citing five additional works: Ok et al. (2016, 2019), Khetan et al. (2017), Zeng et al. (2018), and Kim et al. (2022). It also adds the explicit priority claim. The existing RAG overview largely moves from v4 Appendix D into Section 2.

P1.justification: v5 consolidates related work, adds the noisy-source paragraph, makes limited wording edits, and renumbers subsequent appendices. The author name changes from Junseul Ok to Jungseul Ok. Most prose and the overall scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained, with limited resizing, repositioning, and caption reflow. Examples include Table A1, the placement of Table 3 and Figure 5, and the prompt displays in Figures A6–A7. Plot content and table membership remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly improves scholarly context through the expanded noisy-source literature discussion and consolidates previously separated related work in Section 2. The author-name correction also improves presentation accuracy. These are limited gains: the method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged, and the stronger priority claim alone does not establish better scientific quality.
